title: PMD can never fire on a token the beam top-1 path keeps as original — locally obvious fixes are structurally invisible

repro.actual: only tot->tốt fires; dep->đẹp NEVER suggested although đẹp is the only sensible fix

repro.text: Uu dai dac biet hom nay giam den 50%

expectedVsActual: Emit condition in src/rules/linguistic-rules.mjs requires top1.words[posIdx] !== pos.token.normalized, so only tokens FLIPPED by the global beam can ever be flagged; when the beam keeps the original spelling (originalPriorBonus=0.8 frequently wins globally) the per-position local softmax is never evaluated (verified: no SMS_VAL_DEBUG trace line is printed for such tokens). Corpus impact on the settled snapshot: L05:giam and L10:dep.
disposition: Real engine limitation, not a label error. Suggested direction: evaluate the local softmax for every ambiguous position regardless of the beam choice, or add a second pass over beam-kept ambiguous positions.

severity: MEDIUM (recall gap on clear contexts; precision-first behavior preserved)
title: conf>=0.70 / margin>=0.20 gates reject human-obvious flips when the LM splits probability mass; newly added bare lexicon forms make it worse

repro.note: competes against its own bare form 'ban' (freq 150000)
junk single-letter left neighbor 'h' (from '22h') pollutes bigram context
right neighbor is whitelisted brand 'Tendoo', unknown to LM; từ/tự/tư/tử split
REGRESSION: bare 'gui' entry (freq 150000) + prior bonus makes the model PREFER the wrong unaccented form over gửi (0.024)
REGRESSION: newly added sibling 'toàn' splits mass ('thanh toán gói cước' is unambiguous to humans)

expectedVsActual: All listed corrections are common vocabulary and contextually forced for a human reader, yet every one stayed SILENT. All rejections are precision-safe (zero false positives emitted) but cost recall: 11 tokens across 9 rows on the settled snapshot.
disposition: Direction: grow corpus-train.txt collocation coverage; resolve single-letter junk neighbors away from LM context; reconsider seeding BARE unaccented forms at high frequency (they invert the intended bias, see F4); keep gates otherwise (they held FP at 0).

title: Extra flags beyond expectations were 10/10 contextually CORRECT; hard disambiguation directions were right

extras: trong->trọng ('Tran trong thong bao' -> trân trọng thông báo)

expectedVsActual: Every tolerated extra was correct Vietnamese for its context, including two tricky direction calls: store-hours 'Gio mo cua' resolved to CỬA (door) not CỦA (of, conf=0.999), and 'Thanh toan goi cuoc' correctly KEPT 'thanh' while flagging 'toan' (pre-regression snapshot). Zero wrong-direction flags in 30 rows across all runs.
disposition: No action; recorded as quality evidence for the verdict.

severity: HIGH for reproducibility (data volatility), INFO for labels
title: src/data/lexicon.txt was concurrently rewritten DURING evaluation; measured recall moved 93.6% -> 90.0%, with one transient 82.7% read mid-write
repro: Initial read: 532 lines, no bare 'ban'/'giam'. Settled snapshot at time of writing: 888 lines including bare unaccented entries 'kinh\t150000', 'ban\t150000', 'giam\t150000' and new siblings (toàn, trương, nghỉ...). Same corpus, same code: pre-expansion runs = 103/110 (93.6%, 6x byte-stable); settled post-expansion runs = 99/110 (90.0%, 3x stable); one run that loaded the file DURING rewrite scored 91/110 (82.7%).
expectedVsActual: No expectation in my-corpus.json needed correcting (all 110 judged fair post-hoc via SMS_VAL_DEBUG traces; misses decompose into F1/F2). The bare-form additions REGRESSED PMD recall by flipping previously-won tokens (L06 Gui, L07 Nap, L10 Chuc, L11 mai, L13 toan) through the keep-original bias, while fixing others (L15 hang, L14 Tet). Absolute numbers are only meaningful per lexicon snapshot.
disposition: Evaluator did not modify any protected path. Recommendation: benchmark runs should pin/hash data files (record sha of src/data/* with results.json) and avoid concurrent edits during measurement.

severity: LOW (single occurrence; all later runs deterministic within a snapshot)
title: First-ever harness invocation collapsed (30.9%) and never reproduced; most likely explained by F4-style mid-edit data read
repro: First 'node agent-eval/agent2/run.mjs' reported caught=34/110 with e.g. L02 issues=3 (truth: 11), L03 issues=0 (truth: 6). Immediate rerun plus sequence tests (shared-engine chains, shifted-text interleaves, repeat calls, 6 consecutive full runs) were fully deterministic and correct.
expectedVsActual: Same inputs, different outputs on exactly one process launch. No engine-state leak found (engine verified stateless across validate calls). Most plausible cause: the same concurrent-file-write race documented in F4 (the corpus/data read caught a partially settled state), though not directly observed.
disposition: Not counted against the engine score. Demo-hardening suggestion: boot-time warmup self-check that validates a known sentence and asserts its expected issue count.
